transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-05 16:00 PDT
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nora Kim (Redwood SE), Ivy Chen (Redwood), Janelle Ortiz (Head of Security, Aeon Labs), Ravi Menon (CTO, Aeon Labs), Lucas Greene (Platform Eng), Priya Das (Compliance)
Recording: https://redwood.fireflies/mock/ff-20260705-aeon-09b3

Summary: quick intake to understand Aeon Labs' security gating for hosted vs dedicated vs private; focus areas: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML flows, RBAC requirements, audit log retention, KMS/integrations, encryption at rest/in transit, and data retention rules. Agreed to share artifacts and run Dedicated perf trial.

Topics: SOC2/ISO paperwork, SSO/SAML and IdP flows, RBAC (least privilege), audit trails and log export, KMS options (customer-managed keys), encryption details, retention & purge policies, timeline for POC/benchmarks.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Samir (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call — we got Aeon team?
[00:06] Janelle (Head of Security): Hi, Janelle here. Hi Samir, Nora.
[00:08] Ravi (CTO): Ravi on my side, good to meet you.
[00:11] Lucas (Platform): Lucas — morning.
[00:13] Samir: Awesome. Very high-level — Redwood offers three deployment surfaces: Hosted API for quick time-to-value, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC or on-prem). Today we want to map your security gates so we can recommend the right path. Nora will drive KMS and infra questions.
[00:25] Nora (SE): Hey — thanks. Janelle, can you start with your top 2–3 must-haves from a compliance perspective?
[00:30] Janelle: Sure. We need SOC2 Type II evidence, ideally ISO 27001 certificate as well. Second, SSO via SAML (we use Okta), full audit logs exported to our SIEM, and customer-managed keys for any production PII.
[00:44] Priya (Compliance): Also we have retention constraints — certain PII must be purged after 90 days and we need proof of deletion/retention logs.
[00:52] Nora: Thanks. On SOC2/ISO — we can share our attestation and an SOC2 report with redacted client data. Samir, you'll pull the ISO artifacts right?
[01:00] Samir: Yep, I have those. We'll send SOC2 Type II and ISO cert. Quick note — sometimes the ISO filename comes through as the certification body; we'll include the audit contact if you want.
[01:09] Janelle: Great. For SAML — we want SP-initiated SSO, SCIM for provisioning would be nice. Can we do SAML with Redwood-hosted and also with Dedicated?
[01:20] Nora: Yes. SAML works for Hosted, Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we integrate with standard SAML flows and IdP-initiated is supported; Dedicated and Private can be deployed inside your VPC and point to your IdP for SAML/SCIM endpoints. SCIM provisioning is on our roadmap but we do support manual provisioning + SCIM beta for enterprise customers.
[01:36] Lucas: If we go Dedicated, does our Okta talk directly to the Dedicated pool or is there a proxy? We want no public routing for auth traffic.
[01:45] Nora: For Dedicated we can terminate SAML within your VPC — there's no Internet-exposed auth endpoint. We usually set up an internal endpoint or set up a short-lived nat/elb with strict security groups. There was a note about the 'auth proxy' in older docs — that's legacy; current flows are more direct.
[02:02] Ravi: KMS — we need to use our own AWS KMS CMKs and HSM for keys. Can Redwood use our customer-managed keys for encrypting model cache and logs?
[02:12] Nora: Yes, we support two patterns: 1) Customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for encrypting persisted artifacts, and 2) HSM integration for private deployments. For Hosted we have a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow using a KMS envelope; for Dedicated we can either integrate with your VPC KMS endpoints or configure a remote KMS integration — depends on your networking.
[02:33] Janelle: Does that cover ephemeral KV cache in RAM? We need to ensure nothing sensitive gets flushed to disk or persistent cache.
[02:40] Nora: Our runtime keeps KV cache in-memory; if we spill to disk it's encrypted with your KMS. We can provide the cache lifecycle docs; note that some large-seq workloads cause larger cache usage and we have a config to disable persistent cache.
[02:54] Samir: Quick aside — there might be small transcription: we sometimes see 'KV cash' in older notes — that's K-V cache, not money.
[03:00] (laughs)
[03:03] Janelle: Good to know. On RBAC — we require fine-grained roles: admin, infra, model-ops, dev, read-only, and separate key custody roles. Can Redwood support role scoping and auditable role changes?
[03:17] Nora: Yes — our Console supports RBAC with custom roles and LDAP/SSO mapping. We have an audit log of role changes and can export events to your SIEM. One caveat: For Hosted customers we manage the console; for Dedicated/Private you can host the console in your VPC for stronger control.
[03:34] Lucas: Audit logs — format and retention? We need syslog/JSON events shipped to Splunk.
[03:40] Nora: We can stream audit events via forwarding to AWS Kinesis/CloudWatch, syslog, or direct HTTPS webhook. The events are JSON with fields for actor, action, resource, request_id, and timestamps. For Hosted, retention by default is 90 days, with paid retention add-on. For Dedicated/Private you control retention.
[03:58] Priya: We need immutable tamper-evident logs for at least 13 months for certain regulated workflows. Is write-once storage supported?
[04:06] Nora: For customers needing immutability we support forwarding to your WORM-compliant storage (S3 Object Lock) or external SIEM with immutability. We also sign logs server-side so tamper detection is possible.
[04:18] Janelle: Encryption in transit — TLS v1.2 minimum?
[04:21] Nora: TLS 1.2 minimum and TLS 1.3 preferred. We can enforce TLS ciphers at the load balancer.
[04:28] Ravi: Data residency — our customers in EU require data to stay in eu-west-1. If we use Hosted, can we pin region for storage and inference?
[04:36] Samir: Yes for Hosted you can choose region at org level. We have hosted regions in NA and EU and soon APAC. For strict residency, Dedicated or Private in your VPC is preferred.
[04:45] Lucas: For Private on-prem, how heavy is the install? Are there prebuilt OVA images or a Helm chart?
[04:51] Nora: Private has two install flavors: an on-prem bundle (containerized with Helm manifests) and an air-gapped artifact set. It requires GPUs for inference nodes. We'll share hardware guidance; small clusters start at 4x A10s for evals but production depends on concurrency.
[05:06] Janelle: About evidence — can Redwood provide penetration test results or a red-team summary? We usually require a PTR within the last 12 months.
[05:15] Samir: We maintain a pentest summary and a red-team attestation; we can share the executive summary and findings relevant to infrastructure, redacted. Full reports require NDA.
[05:26] Priya: What about data deletion? We need an API to trigger deletion of historical logs and model inputs and a receipt proving deletion.
[05:35] Nora: We have a delete API and a documented purge workflow; for Hosted we can provide deletion receipts and an audit event. For Dedicated/Private you control the storage and can run the purge locally. We'll document the purge-as-a-service steps.
[05:48] Ravi: Performance — if we go Hosted with encryption and BYOK, any perf hit?
[05:54] Nora: There's a modest latency increase for remote KMS calls — typically single-digit milliseconds per new artifact encrypt/decrypt. For token-level operations we cache DEKs (data encryption keys) to avoid roundtrips, so steady-state latency impact is minimal. We'll validate in the Dedicated trial.
[06:12] Lucas: We'll want a network diagram of the Dedicated topology, with ports, SGs, and egress rules.
[06:18] Nora: We'll share a reference diagram. Also a note on IP allowlisting, we support static egress IPs for some Dedicated clusters or customer-controlled egress via NAT in your VPC.
[06:30] Janelle: Any special certification for cryptographic modules? FIPS?
[06:33] Nora: We support FIPS endpoints (FIPS 140-2) for key operations via certain KMS backends and HSM options for Private deployments. We'll include that in the KMS playbook.
[06:44] Samir: Timeline question — what's your internal timeline for making a decision?
[06:48] Ravi: We're targeting a Q3 pilot. Need security gating cleared by mid-July to kick off a perf POC in August.
[06:56] Samir: Sounds good. We'll aim to get docs to you by next Tuesday. Nora will provision a Dedicated trial for you to run the benchmark.
[07:05] Janelle: On evidence exchange — to whom do we send any signed NDAs if needed for full pentest reports?
[07:10] Samir: Send to legal@redwood.example and cc me. We'll loop in our CISO.
[07:14] Priya: Small note — your older docs sometimes say 'Samlv2' spelled odd, our security scanner flagged metadata mismatches last time; can you ensure metadata endpoints are current?
[07:24] Nora: Yes we'll include updated metadata and a checklist for Okta integration, plus example metadata XML.
[07:31] (brief pause as people skim shared doc link)
[07:40] Lucas: A few gotchas from infra — do model snapshots persist on disk and for how long? We need to ensure any fine-tuned artifacts with customer data are not retained beyond policy.
[07:50] Nora: Model snapshots are versioned; persisted artifacts are encrypted and retention controlled by policy. For Hosted we can set per-organization retention rules; Dedicated you can set retention at cluster level. For anything flagged as customer PII we recommend using Private deployment or Dedicated with strict purge policies.
[08:05] Samir: Ok we're nearing the last few minutes — can we recap next steps?
[08:09] Janelle: Please share SOC2, ISO, pentest summary, KMS playbook, Dedicated topology, and the SAML metadata checklist.
[08:16] Samir: Affirmative. Nora will share architecture/KMS notes and provision a Dedicated trial.
[08:20] Nora: I'll also include a short guide on disabling persistent KV cache and sample audit event payloads for Splunk.
[08:27] Ravi: We'll share retention policy and test dataset.
[08:30] Samir: Great — let's schedule the deep dive for Wed next week, I'll send calendar options.
[08:34] (end-of-meeting housekeeping)
[08:36] Ivy (Redwood): I'll drop links to the security whitepaper, SOC2 attestation, and the Dedicated trial signup in the chat.
[08:42] Janelle: Thanks everyone.
[08:44] Samir: Thanks — talk soon.

Action items (repeated in transcript): Samir to send SOC2 & ISO; Nora to share KMS playbook and Dedicated diagram; Aeon to provide retention policy and dataset; Redwood to provision Dedicated trial.
